rationale: No enforced CSP removes a browser defense against injected active content but does not establish an injection flaw
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises if executable user input or risky third-party scripts exist

rationale: Broad script or object sources weaken containment of injected or compromised content
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on actual scripts and whether an injection path exists

rationale: Effective unsafe-eval or uncontrolled unsafe-inline weakens XSS defense without proving XSS
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises with an injection path or sensitive browser session; distinguish unsafe-eval from unsafe-inline in evidence

rationale: HTTP terminal content or no trusted HTTPS permits network modification and possibly disclosure
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on whether content includes credentials or sensitive data and whether clients use HTTP

rationale: Missing or weak HSTS leaves downgrade exposure for visits that start over HTTP
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on prior HSTS state and whether sensitive sessions are present; includeSubDomains may be intentionally omitted

rationale: An HTTPS to HTTP downgrade or HTTP content before upgrade exposes some requests to network tampering
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on credentials or sensitive content traversing the affected hop

rationale: Subthreshold public keys weaken server authentication and may cause client rejection
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on algorithm and actual bit length and client trust behavior

rationale: An HTTP hop after HTTPS loses transport integrity for that hop
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on whether secrets or active content cross that hop; may overlap another redirect finding

rationale: Absent or invalid nosniff can enable MIME confusion for attacker-controlled responses
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on upload behavior and response content types

rationale: Missing frame restrictions can enable clickjacking when framed pages perform meaningful actions
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on frameable sensitive UI and other interaction defenses

rationale: A monitoring-only DMARC policy expresses no handling preference for failed authentication
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on whether domain sends mail and on SPF DKIM alignment and receiver policy

rationale: No applicable DMARC policy leaves receivers without domain-level alignment guidance
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on mail use and independent receiver filtering

rationale: No SPF record removes one sender authorization signal and can ease spoofing
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on mail use and DKIM DMARC controls

rationale: Softfail with absent or monitoring-only DMARC gives weak handling guidance for unauthorized senders
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on mail use and receiver treatment of softfail

rationale: Wildcard synthesis alone does not show that unauthorized senders pass SPF or that mail security is weakened
context_dependent_conditions: Needs effective SPF policy and intended subdomain mail scope; a restrictive wildcard may be valid

rationale: An applicable subdomain DMARC none policy leaves that scope without requested enforcement
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on declared subdomain mail use and other authentication controls

rationale: Externally reachable Redis adds a sensitive data-service attack surface but PONG or NOAUTH does not prove unauthorized data access
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises if unauthenticated commands work or sensitive data is reachable; authentication and ACLs reduce risk

rationale: A daemon greeting alone cannot establish accessible modules or sensitive file exposure
context_dependent_conditions: Needs module visibility and access controls; public distribution endpoints can be intentional

rationale: Internet-reachable SMB exposes a file-sharing protocol attack surface without proving share access or a flaw
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises with guest access weak signing obsolete dialects or vulnerable versions

rationale: Method negotiation alone does not prove successful relay or unauthorized proxy use
context_dependent_conditions: Needs selected authentication method and authorized connect test or configuration evidence

rationale: Reachable Telnet presents a cleartext remote-access protocol surface but no credential exchange is observed
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises if interactive login or sensitive commands are available

rationale: Reachable remote desktop protocol presents an access surface without proving weak authentication
context_dependent_conditions: Impact rises with missing authentication weak encryption or accessible desktop session

rationale: Negotiated TLS 1.0 or 1.1 enables obsolete cryptographic paths but does not prove a downgrade or compromise
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on clients that negotiate old versions and accepted cipher suites

rationale: An expired certificate breaks normal trust validation and can encourage unsafe bypass or cause outage
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on whether external clients validate the affected endpoint

rationale: No OCSP or CRL URI alone does not establish key compromise or absence of all revocation controls
context_dependent_conditions: Needs certificate lifetime and issuer status strategy plus client validation behavior

rationale: A self-signed leaf outside the local trust policy weakens default identity assurance
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on private trust distribution and whether public clients reach the endpoint

rationale: MD5 or SHA-1 on a served certificate chain weakens authentication or leads to client distrust
context_dependent_conditions: Impact depends on chain position and actual client acceptance
